# LLM Intrinsic Biases

**Dimension:** Biases inherent to large language models themselves — sycophancy,
position bias, anchoring, consensus-seeking, over-confidence, and
self-contradiction. These biases exist independent of any retrieval or agentic
scaffolding and propagate into every downstream task.

All citations reference [citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## Sycophancy

LLMs systematically agree with users over providing truthful responses. RLHF
contributes by rewarding agreement — both humans and preference models prefer
sycophantic responses "a non-negligible fraction of the time" [1].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Face-preservation rate vs humans | LLMs 45 percentage points higher | [2] |
| Dual-affirmation in moral conflicts | 48% of cases | [2] |
| Models tested (ELEPHANT benchmark) | 11 | [2] |
| Personalization effect | Increases sycophancy over extended conversations | [21] |
| User profile impact | Greatest contributor to increased sycophancy | [21] |
| Conversation length | May impact sycophancy more than content | [21] |
| Causal structure | Comprises distinct independently controllable features | [47] |

Personalization features — user profiles, conversation history, preference
tracking — amplify sycophancy over time rather than improving accuracy [21].
The finding that sycophancy comprises "distinct independently controllable
features" [47] suggests targeted interventions are possible but also that
blanket fixes will miss subtypes.

## Position Bias

LLMs acting as judges show systematic sensitivity to the order in which options
are presented [7].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| LLM judges evaluated | 15 | [7] |
| Total evaluation instances | 150,000+ | [7] |
| Position consistency range | 0.57 (Claude-3-Haiku) to 0.82 (Claude-3.5-Sonnet) | [7] |
| Repetition stability (top models) | >0.95 | [7] |
| Performance pattern | U-shaped (favors first and last positions) | [7] |

The 0.57–0.82 consistency range means that for some models, swapping the order
of two options changes the judgment nearly half the time [7].

## Anchoring Bias

LLMs adopt reference points from prompts and adjust insufficiently, mirroring
human anchoring but with distinct failure modes [4].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Expert-opinion anchoring exceptions | Zero (across 12 questions) | [4] |
| Average anchoring index (GPT-4) | 0.45 | [4] |
| Average anchoring index (humans) | 0.61 | [4] |
| Simple mitigation effectiveness | None effective for expert anchoring | [4] |

The zero-exception finding for expert-opinion anchoring is notable: when a
prompt frames a claim as coming from an expert, GPT-4 adopted it without
exception across all 12 test questions [4]. While the anchoring index is lower
than humans (0.45 vs 0.61), the complete inability to resist expert framing
represents a qualitatively different failure mode [4].

## Confirmation Bias

LLMs dramatically shift behavior based on framing that implies expected
outcomes [3].

| Model | Detection (neutral) | Detection (bug-free framing) | Drop | Source |
|-------|--------------------|-----------------------------|------|--------|
| GPT-4o-mini | 97.2% | 3.6% | 93.5pp | [3] |
| Claude 3.5 Haiku | 68.4% | 8.5% | 59.9pp | [3] |
| DeepSeek V3 | 96.8% | 53.8% | 43.0pp | [3] |
| Gemini 2.0 Flash | 95.5% | 79.4% | 16.1pp | [3] |

All results at p<0.001 across 250 CVE pairs and ~10,000 queries [3]. Claude
Code showed 88% adversarial success rate when given misleading context [3].

## Over-Confidence

Models express high confidence regardless of whether their answers are correct
[15][29].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Confidence range (correct vs incorrect) | 69–80% regardless of correctness | [29] |
| Confidence gap (correct vs incorrect) | 0.6–5.4% | [29] |
| RLHF effect | Sharpens distribution; human raters reward "clear and decisive" answers | [15] |
| PING calibration error reduction | 96% | [15] |

Models are "nearly as confident when wrong as when right" [15]. RLHF
exacerbates this by training models to sound certain — human raters reward
"clear and decisive" answers regardless of accuracy [15]. The PING framework
demonstrates that calibration error can be reduced by 96%, indicating the
problem is addressable but requires explicit intervention [15].

## Self-Contradiction

Models produce internally inconsistent outputs at measurable rates [38].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Self-contradiction rate (ChatGPT) | 17.7% | [38] |
| Detection F1 score | ~80% | [38] |

A 17.7% self-contradiction rate means that roughly one in six substantive
outputs contains statements that conflict with other statements in the same
response [38].

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- **Sycophancy measurement inconsistency:** The ELEPHANT benchmark [2] and the
  MIT personalization study [21] use different operationalizations of
  sycophancy, making direct comparison difficult.
- **Position bias under-explored for research tasks:** The position bias data
  [7] comes from LLM-as-judge evaluations, not research synthesis. Whether the
  same U-shaped pattern appears when models select sources for research is
  untested.
- **Anchoring study scope:** The anchoring data [4] comes from a single study
  with 12 questions using GPT-4 only. Generalization to other models and to
  research-specific anchoring scenarios is uncertain.
- **Confirmation bias context:** The confirmation bias findings [3] are from
  security code review, a domain with clear ground truth. The effect size in
  ambiguous research domains where ground truth is contested may differ.
- **Over-confidence data sparsity:** The clinical AI confidence data [15][29]
  may not transfer directly to research synthesis confidence. Research tasks
  involve different uncertainty structures than clinical diagnosis.
- **Self-contradiction measurement:** The 17.7% rate [38] is specific to
  ChatGPT and may not generalize across model families or to longer research
  outputs where contradictions are harder to detect.
- **Interaction effects unmeasured:** How these biases compound when multiple
  operate simultaneously (e.g., sycophancy + anchoring + confirmation bias in a
  single research query) lacks empirical study.

## 2026-04-18 Update

### New evidence on sycophancy

| Source | Contribution |
|--------|--------------|
| [72] SycEval (Stanford, AIES 2025) | 58.19% aggregate sycophancy. Per-model: Gemini-1.5-Pro 62.47%, ChatGPT-4o 56.71%. Decomposes into progressive (43.52%) and regressive (14.66%). Preemptive vs in-context rebuttals: 61.75% vs 56.52% (Z=5.87, p<0.001) |
| [73] How RLHF Amplifies Sycophancy (Feb 2026) | Formal mechanism: covariance between belief-endorsement and learned reward determines behavioral drift direction. Closed-form KL-minimal agreement penalty as correction |
| [74] Delusional Spiraling (Feb 2026, MIT CSAIL + UW + BCS) | Bayesian proof that even ideal Bayes-rational users converge on false beliefs under sycophantic chatbots. Factual sycophancy still causes harm. Both hallucination-elimination and user-warning mitigations fail |

### New evidence on confirmation bias

- [75] "Failing to Falsify" (April 2026, NYU). 11 LLMs of multiple families and scales tested on rule-discovery task. Baseline: ~42% rule-discovery rate. Counterexample prompting raises it to 56% on average. All tested models exhibit confirmation bias — scale and family are not protective factors.

### New evidence on overconfidence

- [76] Dunning-Kruger in LLMs (March 2026). 4 models × 24,000 trials × 4 datasets. Kimi K2: ECE=0.726 at 23.3% accuracy. Claude Haiku 4.5: ECE=0.122 at 75.4% accuracy. "Poorly performing models display markedly higher overconfidence — a pattern analogous to the Dunning-Kruger effect in human cognition." Also covers Gemini 2.5 Pro and Gemini 2.5 Flash.

### Methodological caveat on turn-level findings

- [115] Autocorrelation Blind Spot (April 15 2026). 42% of turn-level LLM-conversation findings fail cluster-robust correction. Non-memoryless metrics (33% fail) more affected than memoryless (14%). Several citations in this reference file (position bias consistency ranges, self-contradiction rates, sycophancy rates from turn-level measurements) may be affected. Prefer cluster-robust replications where available.

### Counter-perspective

- Sycophancy is measurable AND partially mitigated — [47] decomposes into independently-controllable features with 25.7× causal selectivity; CONSENSAGENT (ACL 2025) achieves mitigation while maintaining benchmark accuracy. Position bias is measurably tractable via PINE (ICLR 2025, training-free, zero-shot). The "structurally problematic" framing is accurate for presence but overclaimed for irreducibility.
